source_batch.unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U13: Explain minor benefits and the election on attaining majority

payload.title: Admission to benefits is not full partnership
payload.core_explanation_md:
With all partners consent,a minor may be admitted to the benefits of partnership under the described provision. The minor share is exposed to the firm obligations,but the minor is not personally liable in the same way as a full partner. The minor has the specified account access and a qualified right to sue for a share when severing the connection. Do not call this ordinary admission as a partner.

On majority,the election and public-notice clock runs for six months from the later of attaining majority or obtaining knowledge of the benefits admission. Failure to give the required notice can result in becoming a partner. Electing partnership can bring the described liability for firm acts since benefits admission; electing otherwise has different prospective consequences. Keep the events and notice evidence on a timeline.

self_check.prompt_text: Why is the knowledge date relevant?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The statutory six-month election period uses the later relevant event.

payload.stem_md: A minor admitted to benefits is asked to sign as if already a full personally liable partner. Which distinction is required?

options.text_md: Every beneficiary is automatically a full partner
The minor share can never be affected by firm debts
options.explanation_md: The share has the described exposure.

options.text_md: Benefits admission exposes the share but does not itself create full personal partnership liability
options.explanation_md: Do not replace the special rule with adult partnership assumptions.

options.text_md: No minor can receive any partnership benefit

payload.correct_explanation_md: Do not replace the special rule with adult partnership assumptions.

payload.stem_md: A person learns of their benefits admission only after attaining majority. Which event starts the described election period?

options.text_md: The later of majority and knowledge of the admission
options.explanation_md: The source specifies that later-event rule.

options.text_md: Always the original firm formation date

options.explanation_md: That is not the statutory trigger.
An audit date does not replace the trigger.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The source specifies that later-event rule.
